key_insight: Active learning identified Sn-enriched perovskites with high predicted hydrogen production capacity for chemical looping hydrogen production.
engineering_relevance: Ranking candidates by hydrogen capacity, raw-material price, supply resilience, and potential environmental and health impacts connects materials discovery to deployment needs.
method: Combine a Wasserstein autoencoder with a deep ensemble surrogate model.
Search perovskite compositions autonomously through active learning.
Select 20 diverse candidates using multi-objective ranking.
evidence_signal: Across seven independent 50-cycle runs, mean acquired hydrogen capacity rose from 0.41 to 2.05 mmol H₂/g, with the best compositions reaching 2.65–2.99 mmol H₂/g.
watch_item: The abstract does not report experimental validation or long-term redox cycling stability of the selected candidates.
paper_title: Designing Perovskites for Chemical Looping Hydrogen Production
